holidays.name: National Fluffernutter Day
holidays.description: A salute to the gloriously sticky sandwich of peanut butter and marshmallow creme on soft white bread. It's a lunchbox classic that sits somewhere between sandwich and dessert, and today is the day to have one without guilt.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance. The sandwich itself comes from New England. Marshmallow Fluff was created in Massachusetts in the early 20th century. The Durkee-Mower company of Lynn later popularized the name 'Fluffernutter' in its advertising.
holidays.funFact: Massachusetts lawmakers have debated making the Fluffernutter the official state sandwich, and the proposal has sparked friendly legislative squabbles over the years.

holidays.name: National Pierogi Day
holidays.description: A day for pinching, boiling, and pan-frying these doughy dumplings. Fill them with potato and cheese, sauerkraut, meat, or even sweet fruit, then top them with butter and onions or a big dollop of sour cream.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance. Pierogi are a beloved staple of Polish and wider Eastern European cooking, and the day celebrates that tradition.
holidays.funFact: Saint Hyacinth is traditionally known as the patron saint of pierogi in Poland, and legend ties him to a miraculous supply of the dumplings.

holidays.name: World Octopus Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the eight-armed, shape-shifting, escape-artist geniuses of the sea. Octopuses open jars, squeeze through tiny gaps, and change color and texture in a blink, so this is a day to appreciate one of the ocean's strangest minds.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial awareness observance that grew from online ocean-lover communities. It celebrates octopuses and encourages respect for the animals and their habitats.
holidays.funFact: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood. Two hearts pump blood through the gills, and the third circulates it to the rest of the body.
